President Donald Trump is tweeting out his defiance of the Justice Department's refusal to rule out the possibility that he might pardon himself. It's a bluff, of course. No president may.
The Constitution makes the power to pardon dependent on the president's willingness to exercise it — which means that a president cannot pardon himself if he doesn't want to. The Constitution says nothing about a president pardoning himself and then not having the ability to pardon himself, for example, to avoid prosecution for crimes committed while exercising presidential pardoning power.
The Constitution is very clear about the reason the power was constitutionally delegated to the president in the first place. The framers and ratifiers did not want to rely on the "good will" of the chief executive. They wanted to assure that the president's exercise of his power would not be subject to abuse by a corrupt or unstable president.
